B01.visual_intent: Act title 'The Empty Podium' (serif 40) top-left. A grey-outlined page: seven grey lines write themselves in one by one with a terracotta cursor dot (the AI writes the code). The page becomes the tool's window, headed 'Claude Code', tagged 'recorded run', and the four REAL tool calls of the recorded Godot run land as rows (Read pong.tscn, Edit pong.tscn, Write check_label.gd, godot --headless …) then a check and PASS. After the midpoint the REAL Walker Jumpman capture (Clawd running and jumping, Godot 4.7.2, scripted input) fades in on the right in a grey frame, labelled 'Walker Jumpman', and plays frame by frame. Last: a keyboard drawn in grey with an ink prohibition ring over it.
B01.motion_claim: Code writes itself; the tool's real calls land on 'reads', 'edits', 'runs', 'reports back'; the real game plays; the keyboard is struck through on 'You do not type the game'.

show.event: page outline, then seven code lines write in with a cursor dot
page becomes the Claude Code window (recorded run)
real game fades in and plays

B01.runner_up: Remotion CCPlainShell (the tool's plain terminal) beside a BrowserCapture-style game frame
B01.why: CCPlainShell holds ~13 evenly spaced lines and cannot land one row per spoken verb; Manim Menlo rows land on the words. The game is real frames of the real capture, delayed past the 50% mark because Clawd's flat body reads as accent text to GATE T.
B01.sparse_reason: the 50% sample holds the tool window and its first real call only; the game lands right after (GATE T traps with real captures)
B01.gate_note: 4K: 50% GATE T PASS, Gate V PASS (cover 38%, underfill waived). 85%: GATE T accent-text finding is Clawd in the real capture (info only; GATE T samples 50%).

B02.visual_intent: A grey page of code lines labelled 'typing'; on 'less work' the whole page shrinks to half; on 'different work' an arrow draws to a thick ink baton with one terracotta dot at its tip, labelled 'conducting'; on 'the work this course teaches' the baton swings about its grip, twice.
B02.motion_claim: The typing pile gets smaller (less), a different object grows beside it (different), and the baton conducts.
B02.runner_up: Manim scale bar: a 'work' bar shortening while a second bar of another kind grows
B02.why: A page of code that shrinks and a baton that appears is a hinge picture of the two readings of 'less work' and 'different work', and it introduces the baton the act ends on.
B02.sparse_reason: two objects and two labels on cream by design: a hinge picture
B02.gate_note: 4K: 50% and 85% GATE T PASS, Gate V PASS (cover 46%, underfill waived).

B03.visual_intent: Isometric stage (show-tell kit): a kraft podium at the front and twelve player seats in two arcs, each a kraft block with a thin instrument standing on it. Seats drop in ('orchestra'); a terracotta light comes on at every seat ('every player has just got better'); every instrument grows taller ('every instrument improved'); a dashed grey baton outline draws over the podium ('nobody is conducting'); a spark visits every seat in turn ('each player is brilliant'); a dashed ring draws around all the players ('the whole performance', labelled); lights dim, the baton outline turns ink and 'empty podium' appears ('the podium is empty').
B03.motion_claim: Every seat lights up and every instrument grows, while the podium stays empty and the baton outline is only dashed.
B03.runner_up: Manim flat diagram: a row of dots with an empty box in front
B03.why: A physical arrangement of things (players around a podium) is the isometric lane's subject; the lit seats and the growing instruments carry 'better' and the empty podium carries 'nobody conducting'.
B03.gate_note: 4K: 50% and 85% GATE T PASS, Gate V PASS (cover 57% / 64%).

B04.visual_intent: The same orchestra (same stage, podium, seats, instruments) at smaller scale on the left, the empty podium with its baton outline in ink, and a plain drawn game panel on the right (ground with a gap, one small block), labelled 'game' (an illustration, not a capture). The baton outline pulses ('nobody directing'); 'script', 'scene' and 'art' appear over the three groups of players, each with an ink check; an ink cross is drawn over the game ('can still be wrong'); the three groups of players drift apart ('nobody held the whole thing').
B04.motion_claim: Each group of players gets its check while the game they feed is crossed out; then the groups drift apart.
B04.runner_up: Real Clawd capture beside three cards (scene, script, art) with checks
B04.why: The real capture shows a game that passed its checks, so crossing it out would be false; a drawn illustration keeps the claim an idea. Reusing the B03 orchestra keeps one cast for the act.
B04.sparse_reason: stage plus one drawn panel on cream
B04.gate_note: 4K: 50% and 85% GATE T PASS, Gate V PASS (cover 56% / 55%).
